landmarks.name: Grand Central Terminal
landmarks.street_address: 71-105 East 42nd Street; visitor site also publishes 89 E 42nd Street, New York, NY 10017
landmarks.description: Historic rail terminal completed in 1913, combining monumental Beaux-Arts design and a major transportation function.
landmarks.architectural_relevance: The NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission describes it as a magnificent example of French Beaux-Arts architecture and an artistic solution to a difficult engineering problem.
landmarks.historical_relevance: The present terminal was completed in 1913 after the earlier Grand Central Depot; the development helped shape Midtown and Terminal City.
source_type: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designation report

landmarks.name: Pershing Square Building
landmarks.street_address: 125 Park Avenue (also 101-105 East 41st Street, 100-108 East 42nd Street, 117-123 and 127-131 Park Avenue)
landmarks.description: A 1921-23 office building at Park Avenue and East 42nd Street, opposite Grand Central Terminal.
landmarks.architectural_relevance: LPC describes its Lombard Revival design, colorful brick and terra-cotta facades, and distinctive tower form without the later setback profile.
landmarks.historical_relevance: Its site and foundations were linked to subway construction; the building became part of Terminal City's redevelopment around Grand Central.
source_type: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designation report

landmarks.name: Chrysler Building
landmarks.description: A landmark Midtown skyscraper known for its Art Deco design and distinctive crown.
landmarks.architectural_relevance: The NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designated the Chrysler Building as an individual landmark; its designation report documents its design and fabric.
landmarks.historical_relevance: Constructed during the late-1920s Manhattan skyscraper boom and associated with automobile executive Walter P. Chrysler.
source_type: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designation report

landmarks.name: Graybar Building
landmarks.street_address: 420 Lexington Avenue (aka 420-430 Lexington Avenue), New York, NY 10170
landmarks.description: A 1925-27 office building associated with Grand Central's Terminal City development.
landmarks.architectural_relevance: LPC identifies its Art Deco and Byzantine decorative program, stepped form, monumental reliefs, and sculpted rat details at the portals.
landmarks.historical_relevance: One of the final Terminal City structures; it housed Graybar Electric's headquarters from 1927 to 1982 and was designated a city landmark in 2016.
source_type: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designation report

landmarks.name: Chanin Building
landmarks.street_address: 122 East 42nd Street (aka 374 Lexington Avenue), New York, NY
landmarks.description: A 1927-29 Art Deco office skyscraper at Lexington Avenue and East 42nd Street.
landmarks.architectural_relevance: An Art Deco tower designed by Sloan & Robertson with sculptural decoration by Rene Chambellan.
landmarks.historical_relevance: Part of the 1920s Midtown high-rise development around Grand Central Terminal.
source_type: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission project presentation

landmarks.name: Daily News Building
landmarks.description: A Raymond Hood-designed Art Deco skyscraper originally built as the headquarters of the Daily News.
landmarks.architectural_relevance: A major Art Deco presence with a notable lobby and globe; the exterior and first-floor interior have landmark status.
landmarks.historical_relevance: Built in 1929-30 as home and symbol of the Daily News; it is also a National Historic Landmark.

landmarks.name: 1 Vanderbilt
landmarks.street_address: 1 Vanderbilt Avenue, Manhattan, New York City
landmarks.description: A Midtown Manhattan office and observation tower at 1 Vanderbilt Avenue.
landmarks.architectural_relevance: Contemporary supertall office tower with a tapered profile and articulated crown.
landmarks.historical_relevance: Developed as part of the East Midtown commercial district adjacent to Grand Central Terminal.
source_type: official building website; descriptive details require further source review

landmarks.name: Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
landmarks.street_address: 476 Fifth Avenue, Manhattan, New York City
landmarks.description: The New York Public Library's landmark main research library on Fifth Avenue at Bryant Park.
landmarks.architectural_relevance: A major Beaux-Arts civic building designed by Carrere and Hastings.
landmarks.historical_relevance: Opened in 1911 as the New York Public Library's central research library.
source_type: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designation report

landmarks.name: Bryant Park
landmarks.street_address: Between West 40th and West 42nd Streets and Fifth and Sixth Avenues, New York, NY
landmarks.description: A major public park in Midtown Manhattan behind the NYPL Stephen A. Schwarzman Building.
landmarks.architectural_relevance: A large urban public space with recurring programming and amenities; it occupies the public-landscape side of this route's destination area.
landmarks.historical_relevance: The site has served as a potter's field, was associated with the Croton Reservoir era, and underwent restoration efforts led by Bryant Park Corporation, founded in 1980.
